source.text_it: Nel caso di una emorragia esterna arteriosa bisogna lasciare defluire tutto il sangue

records.localized_text: For external arterial bleeding, allow all the blood to drain.

source.text_it: Nel caso di emorragia esterna bisogna evitare qualsiasi intervento

records.localized_text: For external bleeding, avoid any intervention.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente stradale presenta una ferita sanguinante non bisogna intervenire se l'infortunato è in stato di ebbrezza

records.localized_text: If a road accident victim has a bleeding wound, do not intervene if the casualty is intoxicated.

source.text_it: Per arrestare un'emorragia esterna arteriosa è sufficiente un cerotto

records.localized_text: A plaster is sufficient to stop external arterial bleeding.

source.text_it: Nel caso di una emorragia esterna arteriosa bisogna arrestare la fuoriuscita del sangue il prima possibile

records.localized_text: For external arterial bleeding, stop the blood loss as soon as possible.

source.text_it: Cinture o cravatte sono utilizzabili come laccio emostatico da porre a monte della ferita per ridurre una emorragia arteriosa

records.localized_text: Belts or ties may be used as a tourniquet above the wound to reduce arterial bleeding.

source.text_it: È opportuno che il soccorritore si protegga dal contatto con il sangue dell'infortunato utilizzando guanti o altri mezzi

records.localized_text: The rescuer should protect against contact with the casualty's blood using gloves or other means.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente stradale presenta una ferita sanguinante bisogna allargare la ferita per fare uscire il pus

records.localized_text: If a road accident victim has a bleeding wound, enlarge it to let pus out.

source.text_it: L'emorragia esterna venosa comporta il rischio di soffocamento

records.localized_text: External venous bleeding poses a risk of suffocation.

source.text_it: Per ridurre una emorragia esterna venosa, è utile tamponare a pressione la ferita con materiale possibilmente sterile

records.localized_text: To reduce external venous bleeding, apply pressure to the wound with preferably sterile material.

source.text_it: Nel caso di emorragia esterna venosa, bisogna immediatamente anestetizzare l'infortunato

records.localized_text: For external venous bleeding, immediately anaesthetise the injured person.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente stradale presenta una ferita sanguinante bisogna intervenire con materiale quanto più possibile pulita

records.localized_text: If a road accident victim has a bleeding wound, use material that is as clean as possible.

source.text_it: Nel caso di emorragia venosa il sangue esce zampillando

records.localized_text: In venous bleeding, blood spurts out.

source.text_it: Per ridurre una emorragia esterna venosa sono utili impacchi di acqua fredda o ghiaccio

records.localized_text: Cold-water or ice packs are useful to reduce external venous bleeding.

source.text_it: Se la vittima di un incidente presenta una abbondante emorragia bisogna chiamare al più presto l'ambulanza

records.localized_text: If an accident victim is bleeding heavily, call an ambulance as soon as possible.

source.text_it: Nel caso di emorragia arteriosa il sangue fluisce con continuità

records.localized_text: In arterial bleeding, blood flows continuously.

source.text_it: Nel caso di una emorragia esterna arteriosa si determina il rischio di una rapida morte per dissanguamento

records.localized_text: External arterial bleeding carries a risk of rapid death from blood loss.

source.text_it: L'emorragia esterna venosa è caratterizzata dal fatto che il sangue esce senza zampillare

records.localized_text: External venous bleeding is characterised by blood flowing without spurting.

source.text_it: Se la ferita ha tracce di terra, occorre lavarla con acqua

records.localized_text: If a wound contains traces of soil, wash it with water.

source.text_it: L'emorragia esterna arteriosa è caratterizzata dal fatto che il sangue esce zampillando a schizzi intermittenti

records.localized_text: External arterial bleeding is characterised by intermittent spurts of blood.

source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole la vittima proverà dolore nella respirazione

records.localized_text: With fractured ribs, the victim will feel pain while breathing.

source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole, ove non ci siano lesioni alla schiena, bisogna spostare la vittima

records.localized_text: With fractured ribs, move the victim if there are no back injuries.

source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole l'infortunato deve essere tenuto in posizione semiseduta se è cosciente

records.localized_text: A conscious person with fractured ribs must be kept in a semi-seated position.

source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole, se la vittima non respira, bisogna astenersi dall'intervenire

records.localized_text: If a person with fractured ribs is not breathing, refrain from intervening.

source.text_it: In caso di frattura delle costole bisogna evitare il più possibile che l'infortunato si muova

records.localized_text: With fractured ribs, avoid the casualty moving as much as possible.

rows.text: Severe arterial bleeding can quickly cause fatal shock. Apply pressure to the wound immediately and call emergency services.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Do not remain inactive: apply pressure to the wound with clean material and call emergency services immediately if bleeding is severe.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Intoxication does not remove the need for help: control the bleeding with pressure on the wound and protect yourself from contact with blood.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: A plaster will not necessarily control severe arterial bleeding. Apply firm pressure to the wound and call emergency services immediately.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Severe blood loss can quickly cause shock. Apply pressure to the wound immediately and call emergency services.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: The quiz marks this TRUE, but not every belt or tie is suitable. For life-threatening limb bleeding, a commercial tourniquet is preferred; if unavailable, only in an emergency can broad cloth be used for a correctly constructed improvised tourniquet. A leather belt may not work: call emergency services and follow their instructions.
evidence: Official CQC 31680 printed VERO: belts or ties as tourniquets; material, technique and severity are not specified.

AHA/Red Cross 2024 first aid guidelines https://cpr.heart.org/en/resuscitation-science/2024-first-aid-guidelines — for life-threatening extremity bleeding commercial tourniquet preferred; improvised at least 2 inches wide.

FEMA TECC module 4 https://emilms.fema.gov/training/microlearning/tecc_familiarization/assets/FCC5D96D-A03B-5B20-AEDD-20A80292F7F2/TECC%20Transcript.html — mass-casualty context, cloth necktie with windlass possible, stiff leather belt unsuitable; not a general instruction to use every belt.

rows.text: Gloves or another waterproof barrier reduce contact with blood and the risk of transmitting infection while providing aid.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Do not enlarge a bleeding wound: instead try to control bleeding with pressure and clean material.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: The danger inherent in severe venous bleeding is blood loss and possible shock, not choking. Any airway problems still need separate assessment.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Direct pressure with a sterile dressing, if available, helps reduce blood loss from the wound.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Anaesthesia does not stop bleeding. First apply pressure to the wound and seek emergency help if bleeding is severe.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: A clean, preferably sterile dressing helps protect the wound while pressure is applied to control bleeding.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Venous blood generally flows steadily; pulsating spurts are typical of arterial bleeding. Either can be serious.
evidence: New York Naval Militia, MEBS SEA-MAN, p. 173, https://dmna.ny.gov/forms/naval/NYNMINST_3120_2_MEBS_Seamanship_Manual.pdf — arterial blood spurts with the pulse; venous blood typically flows steadily; serious bleeding requires urgent control.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE: direct pressure is needed to control a bleeding wound; cold is not a reliable substitute. This does not mean cold can never affect blood vessels. If bleeding is severe, call emergency services immediately.
evidence: Official CQC 31688 printed FALSO: asks whether cold water or ice is useful to reduce external venous bleeding, without specifying severity; available guidelines support direct pressure, not a proof that cold has zero vascular effect.

ANZCOR guideline 9.1.1 https://www.anzcor.org/home/first-aid/guideline-9-1-1-first-aid-for-management-of-bleeding — firm direct pressure for external bleeding; severe limb bleeding may need tourniquet.

rows.text: Heavy blood loss can quickly cause shock. Call emergency services immediately and apply pressure to the wound.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE: arterial blood may spurt with the heartbeat, unlike the generally steadier flow from a vein. “Continuous” is ambiguous: arterial blood does not have to stop between beats. Treat severe bleeding immediately without waiting to identify the vessel.
evidence: Official CQC 31690 printed FALSO: continuous flow has no explicit definition; interpreting it as nonpulsatile uniform flow is a teaching interpretation, not an established official rationale.

New York Naval Militia MEBS SEA-MAN printed p.173 PDF index172 https://dmna.ny.gov/forms/naval/NYNMINST_3120_2_MEBS_Seamanship_Manual.pdf — arterial jets synchronized to pulse versus steady venous flow; no assertion that flow must stop between pulses.

American Red Cross https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — continuous or spurting blood can signal life-threatening bleeding; immediate pressure and emergency help.

rows.text: An arterial injury can cause rapid, extensive blood loss and fatal shock; control the bleeding immediately and call emergency services.
evidence: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Venous blood generally flows without the pulsating spurts typical of arterial blood. Heavy venous bleeding remains an emergency.
evidence: New York Naval Militia, MEBS SEA-MAN, p. 173, https://dmna.ny.gov/forms/naval/NYNMINST_3120_2_MEBS_Seamanship_Manual.pdf — arterial blood spurts with the pulse; venous blood typically flows steadily; serious bleeding requires urgent control.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.

rows.text: After bleeding has stopped, a small dirty wound can be rinsed with clean water to remove dirt; seek medical assessment if it remains dirty.
evidence: NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — pressure with clean material, cleaning after bleeding stops, and urgent care for serious wounds.

rows.text: Arterial blood can emerge in pulsating jets synchronized with the heartbeat. Such bleeding requires immediate control and urgent help.
evidence: New York Naval Militia, MEBS SEA-MAN, p. 173, https://dmna.ny.gov/forms/naval/NYNMINST_3120_2_MEBS_Seamanship_Manual.pdf — arterial blood spurts with the pulse; venous blood typically flows steadily; serious bleeding requires urgent control.

American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — direct pressure, emergency help, shock and barrier protection.

rows.text: A broken rib can cause chest pain, particularly when the chest moves during inhalation or coughing.
evidence: NHS, Broken or bruised ribs, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/broken-or-bruised-ribs/ — pain on breathing; serious accident and worsening breathing need urgent assessment.

rows.text: Call emergency services. The absence of a known back injury does not itself require moving the person: avoid unnecessary movement, but move them if necessary for safety, CPR or control of life-threatening bleeding. Follow the dispatcher’s instructions.
evidence: American Red Cross, Chest Injury, General Care and positioning FAQ, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/chest-injury — allow responsive person a position of comfort; if head, neck or back injury suspected, leave as found unless movement needed for safety, CPR or bleeding control; monitor and seek emergency assistance. A semi-seated position is a possible comfort position, not a mandatory position.

rows.text: A conscious person with a chest injury may find a semi-seated position more comfortable; do not force it. If a head, neck or back injury is suspected, avoid moving them unless necessary for safety or lifesaving care, and follow emergency instructions.
evidence: American Red Cross, Chest Injury, General Care and positioning FAQ, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/chest-injury — allow responsive person a position of comfort; if head, neck or back injury suspected, leave as found unless movement needed for safety, CPR or bleeding control; monitor and seek emergency assistance. A semi-seated position is a possible comfort position, not a mandatory position.

rows.text: If the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally, call emergency services and begin CPR: a suspected fracture does not justify inaction.
evidence: NHS 111 Wales, First aid, https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — call emergency services and start CPR if unresponsive and not breathing normally; suspected spinal injury requires care with movement.

rows.text: While waiting for emergency services, avoid unnecessary movement after trauma, keep the person comfortable and monitor breathing.
evidence: St John Ambulance, Broken Bones and Fractures, https://www.sja.org.uk/first-aid-advice/fractures-and-broken-bones/ — keep still and support injury; move in immediate danger.

NHS 111 Wales, First aid, https://111.wales.nhs.uk/encyclopaedia/f/article/firstaid/ — call emergency services and start CPR if unresponsive and not breathing normally; suspected spinal injury requires care with movement.

source_access_notes: Independently inspected New York Naval Militia manual p.173 for arterial pulsatile vs venous steady flow, AHA/Red Cross 2024 severe bleeding guideline, ANZCOR 9.1.1, NHS rib care and American Red Cross chest-injury first aid. 31680 qualified improvised tourniquet, 31688 cold not substitute for pressure, and 31690 ambiguous continuity all passed.

Rechecked Red Cross chest injury general care and position-of-comfort FAQ; revised 31696 calls emergency services unconditionally and allows needed movement for safety, CPR and bleeding control; 31697 describes semi-seated as a possible comfort choice with head/neck/back precautions.

issues.reason: Il verdetto VERO presenta cinture o cravatte come lacci utilizzabili senza condizioni: non è verificata l’efficacia specifica di entrambe né la compatibilità di tale indicazione generica con le raccomandazioni attuali.
checked_sources: American Red Cross, 2020 Focused Updates and Guidelines, First Aid p. 16, https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/training-services/sac/docs/American%20Red%20Cross%20Focused%20Updates%20and%20Guidelines%202020.pdf — preferisce dispositivi commerciali e considera lacci improvvisati per soccorritori addestrati solo in condizioni specifiche.

American Red Cross, How to Apply a Tourniquet, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/articles/how-to-apply-a-tourniquet — laccio per emorragia pericolosa di un arto, sopra la ferita, e pressione diretta.

issues.reason: Il verdetto FALSO nega senza qualifiche l’utilità di freddo o ghiaccio per ridurre una emorragia venosa esterna; la priorità della pressione non dimostra che il freddo non possa essere utile. Non è stata verificata un’autorità che risolva la formulazione assoluta.
checked_sources: American Red Cross, Bleeding, Life-Threatening External, https://www.redcross.org/take-a-class/resources/learn-first-aid/bleeding-life-threatening-external — raccomanda pressione diretta e soccorso urgente, senza pronunciarsi sull’utilità del freddo.
NHS, Cuts and grazes, https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/cuts-and-grazes/ — indica pressione sulla ferita per controllare il sanguinamento, senza escludere ogni utilità del freddo.

issues.reason: Il verdetto FALSO afferma implicitamente una distinzione assoluta, ma il testo non precisa che il flusso è continuo e non pulsante; un flusso arterioso può essere continuo e pulsante. Serve verificare il significato previsto prima di attribuire alla frase una limitazione assente.
checked_sources: New York Naval Militia, MEBS SEA-MAN, p. 173, https://dmna.ny.gov/forms/naval/NYNMINST_3120_2_MEBS_Seamanship_Manual.pdf — descrive getti arteriosi sincronizzati con il battito e flusso venoso continuo.
USU Stop the Bleed, https://stopthebleed.usuhs.edu/ — descrive perdita di sangue che fluisce continuamente e può anche zampillare.

issues.reason: Immediate danger is presented as the sole exception to avoiding movement. Red Cross chest injury guidance also allows movement necessary for CPR or life-threatening bleeding control. Clarify lifesaving exceptions and follow dispatcher; English/Chinese syntax also risks making the instruction to call for help conditional on absence of danger.

NHS rib page discusses sleeping more upright during recovery but does not establish semi-sitting first aid at an accident. Cite directly inspected applicable first-aid source for chest-injury positioning or scope learner text to a conscious patient’s comfortable position, with injury precautions.
